citation: Lee, H. (2010). Infrastructure interdependencies simulation (I2Sim) system model and toolbox. University of British Columbia. doi:10.14288/1.0064885
description: I2Sim is an infrastructure interdependencies simulator developed by the University of British Columbia group led by José Martí under Canada's Joint Infrastructure Interdependencies Research Program, which was selected to build a simulator for the Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics. It represents infrastructure with cells, channels and tokens, where Human Readable Tables describe the relation between each unit's inputs and outputs, so that reasonable predictions can be made with limited data and without owners disclosing confidential operational information. A 2010 UBC master's thesis by HyunJung Lee documents the system model and a customised MATLAB/Simulink toolbox with a drag-and-drop graphical interface, adding channel time delays and human flow, and test cases built for the UBC campus and extended to Olympic sites in Vancouver, used to derive optimal resource allocation and restoration priorities during disasters. The thesis is accessible through UBC's open collections repository; the toolbox itself is not published there and no licence is stated. Caveats: the documentation dates from 2010, the software requires MATLAB/Simulink, and the UBC site blocked automated access when checked. It supports cascading failure, interdependency, emergency response and optimisation modelling; a related record is the INL CIMS critical infrastructure modelling system.
